Key computation: for $\mathcal G=(B,\psi,A)$ with $B=\bigoplus_{k=1}^mM_{n(k)}(\mathbb C)$, writing $S^{(k)}=(\dim B/n(k))[S(e_{ij}^{(k)})]$ turns the defining relation $\mu(1\otimes\mu)(S\otimes S^*\otimes S)(1\otimes m^*)m^*=S$ into $S^{(k)}S^{(k)*}S^{(k)}=S^{(k)}$, while $\mu(S^*\otimes S)m^*=\mu(S\otimes S^*)m^*A$ becomes $S^{(k)*}S^{(k)}=(S^{(1)}S^{(1)*},\ldots,S^{(m)}S^{(m)*})\widetilde A$; these relations define $\mathcal O_{\mathcal G}$, give $\mathcal O_{\mathcal G}$ equal to the usual Cuntz--Krieger algebra when $B$ is abelian, and for the complete quantum graph yield the explicit quotient $\mathcal O_{K(M_n)}\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal O_{n^2}$ by $S_{ij}\mapsto n^{-1/2}\widehat S_{ij}$.

title: Dominic Joyce
note: Dominic Joyce, global quotient stacks form a $(2,1)$-category in which classifying stacks retain automorphisms of principal bundles and $2$-fibre products differ essentially from fibre products in the homotopy category. Key computation: morphisms $U\to[*/\Gamma]$ classify principal $\Gamma$-bundles $P\to U$, and the fibre product of $[U/\Gamma]\to[W/K]\leftarrow[V/\Delta]$ is $[\{(u,v,k):f(u)=kg(v)\}/(\Gamma\times\Delta)]$ with $(\gamma,\delta)(u,v,k)=(\gamma u,\delta v,\rho(\gamma)k\sigma(\delta)^{-1})$; in particular $*\times_{[*/\Gamma]}*\simeq\Gamma$, so pulling back the tautological $*\to[*/\Gamma]$ along the classifying map recovers $P\to U$.

title: Dominic Joyce
note: Dominic Joyce, coherent sheaves on $\mathbb{CP}^1$ are classified by line bundles and finite-length skyscraper sheaves, and torsion-free sheaves compactify moduli of vector bundles by admitting singular limits. Key computation: the exact sequence $0\to\mathcal O_{\mathbb{CP}^1}\xrightarrow{s^{\otimes k}}\mathcal O_{\mathbb{CP}^1}(k)\to\mathcal O_{[x,y]}^{(k)}\to0$ constructs the length-$k$ torsion summands, and every $E\in\operatorname{coh}(\mathbb{CP}^1)$ decomposes uniquely as a finite direct sum of $\mathcal O_{\mathbb{CP}^1}(n)$ and $\mathcal O_{[x,y]}^{(k)}$; on $\mathbb{CP}^2$, the cokernel of $(y,z,\delta\operatorname{id}):\mathcal O\to\mathcal O(1)^{\oplus2}\oplus\mathcal O$ is $\mathcal O(1)^{\oplus2}$ for $\delta\ne0$ but specializes at $\delta=0$ to $(I_{[1,0,0]}\otimes\mathcal O(2))\oplus\mathcal O$, an explicit non-locally-free torsion-free limit.

title: Dominic Joyce
note: Dominic Joyce, Dwyer--Kan hammock localization upgrades inversion of weak equivalences from an ordinary homotopy category to a simplicial model for the associated $\infty$-category, while horn filling distinguishes categories, groupoids, and quasicategories. Key computation: for a model category $\mathcal M$, the mapping simplicial set $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{DK}}(X,Y)$ is built from rows of zigzags $X\leftarrow^{\sim}K_1\leftarrow^{\sim}L_1\to K_2\leftarrow^{\sim}\cdots\to Y$, and $\pi_0\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{DK}}(X,Y)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M[W^{-1}]}(X,Y)$; moreover a simplicial set is $N(\mathcal C)$ exactly when every inner horn has a unique filler, and $N(\mathcal C)$ is Kan exactly when $\mathcal C$ is a groupoid, identifying Kan complexes as models for $\infty$-groupoids and weak Kan complexes as quasicategories.

title: Dominic Joyce
note: Dominic Joyce, PTVV shifted symplectic structures turn Calabi--Yau moduli into explicit local critical-locus geometry and lower the shift under derived Lagrangian intersection. Key computation: for the derived moduli stack $\mathcal M$ of coherent complexes on a Calabi--Yau $m$-fold, $h^i(T_{\mathcal M}|_E)\cong\operatorname{Ext}^{i+1}(E,E)$ and Serre duality $\operatorname{Ext}^i(E,E)\cong\operatorname{Ext}^{m-i}(E,E)^*$ induce the nondegenerate quasi-isomorphism $T_{\mathcal M}\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{\mathcal M}[2-m]$, hence a $(2-m)$-shifted symplectic form; if $L,M\to(X,\omega_k)$ are Lagrangian then $L\times_XM$ is $(k-1)$-shifted symplectic, and for $k=-1$ the shifted Darboux theorem gives $(X,\omega)\simeq\operatorname{Crit}(H:U\to\mathbb A^1)$ Zariski locally, so Calabi--Yau $3$-fold sheaf moduli are locally classical critical loci.

title: Jared Weinstein
note: Jared Weinstein, Faltings's two-towers theorem identifies the Lubin--Tate and Drinfeld towers as quotient $v$-stacks and converts Morava-stabilizer cohomology into $p$-adic Lie-group cohomology. Key computation: the isomorphism $[\mathrm{LT}_{n,\eta}^{\diamond}/\mathbb G_n]\cong[\mathcal H_{n-1}^{\diamond}/\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb Z_p)]$ arises because a height-$n$, dimension-$1$ $p$-divisible group $G/\mathcal O_C$ has Hodge--Tate sequence $0\to\operatorname{Lie}G\otimes C(1)\to T_pG\otimes C\to(\operatorname{Lie}G^*)^*\otimes C\to0$, determining a line in $T_pG\otimes C$, with the formal-group locus exactly Drinfeld's $\mathcal H_{n-1}$; taking $\mathcal O^+$-cohomology yields $H^*(\mathbb G_n,W(\mathbb F_p))\to H^*(\mathbb G_n,W(\mathbb F_p)[[u_1,\ldots,u_{n-1}]])$ as an isomorphism after inverting $p$ and $H^*(\mathbb G_n,E_n^0)[1/p]\cong\mathbb Q_p[x_1,x_3,\ldots,x_{2n-1}]$ with $|x_i|=i$.

title: Dihua Jiang
note: Dihua Jiang, consecutive local descents of enhanced Langlands parameters classify the arithmetic wavefront set of generic representations of classical groups by rational nilpotent orbits. Key computation: local Gan--Gross--Prasad gives $\dim_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Hom}_{M_{\ell,X}}(J_X(V_\pi)\otimes\widehat\sigma^\vee,1)=1$ exactly when the component-group characters satisfy $(\chi,\chi')=(\chi^z_{\phi,\varphi},\chi^z_{\varphi,\phi})$; defining $D_\ell(\phi,\chi)=\bigcup_{z\in F^\times/F^{\times2}}D_\ell^z(\phi,\chi)$ and $\ell_0=\max\{\ell:D_\ell(\phi,\chi)\ne\varnothing\}$, first descent is discrete and $\ell_0(\pi)=\ell_0(\phi,\chi)$, so iteration produces signed Young-tableau data $(\ell_j,q(\ell_j))$ and a canonical orbit set $\mathrm{WF}_{\mathrm{ari}}(\pi)$; over $\mathbb R$, if $S_\phi\ne1$ then $\mathrm{WF}_{\mathrm{ari}}(\pi)_{\max}=\{\mathcal O_a(\phi,\chi)\}$, a unique rational nilpotent orbit determining a stable orbit.

title: Wee Teck Gan
note: Wee Teck Gan, the endoscopic classification of the metaplectic group $\operatorname{Mp}_{2n}$ decomposes its discrete automorphic spectrum into packets indexed by elliptic Arthur parameters, with multiplicities controlled by component-group characters and central epsilon factors. Key computation: for $\Psi=\boxplus_i\Pi_i\boxtimes S_{d_i}$ the local packet is $\widetilde\Pi_{\Psi_v,\psi_v}=\bigoplus_{\eta_v\in\operatorname{Irr}(S_{\Psi_v})}\eta_v\otimes\widetilde\pi_{\eta_v}$ and $\widetilde A_{n,\mathrm{disc}}=\bigoplus_\Psi\widetilde A_{\Psi,\psi}$ with $\widetilde A_{\Psi,\psi}=\langle\widetilde\epsilon_\Psi,\Delta^*(\widetilde\Pi_{\Psi,\psi})\rangle_{S_\Psi}$, where $\widetilde\epsilon_\Psi=\epsilon_\Psi\widetilde\eta_\Psi$ and $\widetilde\eta_\Psi(e_i)=\epsilon(1/2,\Pi_i)$ for symplectic $\Pi_i$ and $1$ for orthogonal $\Pi_i$; locally, endoscopic transfer satisfies $t_{a,b}^*(\Theta_\Psi)=\epsilon(1/2,\Psi_b)\sum_\eta\eta(s_{a,b})\Theta_{\widetilde\pi_\eta}$ for $s_{a,b}=(1_{2a},-1_{2b})$.

title: Yiannis Sakellaridis (joint with Chen Wan)
note: Yiannis Sakellaridis (joint with Chen Wan), comparison of the Jacquet--Zagier and Kuznetsov trace formulas separates the residual spectrum of $\mathrm{GL}_n$ into boundary terms indexed by generic length. Key computation: after partially compactifying Whittaker test functions there is an isomorphism $U:\mathcal S(G/G)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal S^+((N,\psi)\backslash G/(N,\psi))$ pulling stable characters back to relative characters and satisfying $\mathrm{STF}(f)=\mathrm{KTF}(Uf)+\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}B_j(f)$; the Kuznetsov main term has spectral expansion over generic automorphic representations, whereas $B_j$ has expansion over representations of generic length $n-j$, and meromorphic comparison in a parameter $s$ pairs the divergence of the naive trace formula with the pole of $L(\pi,\operatorname{Ad},s)$, so taking $\operatorname{Res}_{s=1}$ yields the noninvariant trace-formula identity with all residual boundary contributions separated.

title: Bill Casselman
note: Bill Casselman, the inverse Satake transform gives an explicit basic Schwartz function for every irreducible finite-dimensional representation of $\widehat{\mathrm{GL}}_2$, reducing the construction to symmetric-power multiplicities and vector partition functions. Key computation: for $F_{m,n}=\mathbf1_{K\varpi^{(m,n)}K}$, $\mathcal S^{-1}(\det^nq^{(m-n)/2}\chi_{m-n})=\Phi_{m,n}=\sum_{i:m-i\ge n+i}F_{m-i,n+i}$, while $\det(I-At)^{-1}=\sum_{m\ge0}\operatorname{tr}S^m(A)t^m$ and $S^m(\sigma_k)=\sum_{i\le km/2}\delta_{km}(i)\det^i\sigma_{km-2i}$ imply that the $L$-function's basic function is $\sum_{i\le km/2}q^i\delta_{km}(i)\Phi_{km-i,i}$; writing the weight multiplicity piecewise as $\omega_{km}(n)=\sum_{j=0}^i(-1)^jD_{\alpha_j}(n-m_j)$ on $m_i\le n\le m_{i+1}$ proves it is quasi-polynomial on each Sturmfels cone and yields the displayed Sylvester asymptotics for $\omega_{km}$ and $\delta_{km}$.

title: Malors Espinosa (joint with Melissa Emory
note: Malors Espinosa (joint with Melissa Emory, Debanjana Kundu, and Tian An Wong), interpolation and Poisson summation isolate the trivial and special-representation traces inside the regular elliptic trace formula for $\mathrm{GL}_2$ over a totally real number field. Key computation: contributing elliptic classes are exactly $(\tau,u)\in\mathcal O_K\times\mathcal O_K^\times$ with $\tau^2-4u\epsilon$ nonsquare, and $(\tau^2-4u\epsilon)=\mathfrak S_\gamma^2\Delta_\gamma$ defines $O(z,\gamma)=N(\mathfrak S_\gamma)^z\sum_{\mathfrak d\mid\mathfrak S_\gamma}N(\mathfrak d)^{1-2z}\prod_{\mathfrak q\mid\mathfrak d'}(1-\chi_\gamma(\mathfrak q)N(\mathfrak q)^{-z})$; then $O(1,\gamma)=\prod_{\mathfrak q}O(\gamma,f_\mathfrak q)$ and $\Lambda(z,\chi_\gamma)O(z,\gamma)=\Lambda(1-z,\chi_\gamma)O(1-z,\gamma)$, while Poisson summation gives $\operatorname{Tr}(1(f))=p^{-k/2}(1-p^{-(k+1)})(1-p^{-1})^{-1}\sum_\pm\int_{\mathbb R^{2n-1}}\theta_\pm(x,y)\,dx\,dy$ and identifies the second residue as $-2$ times the special-representation trace.

title: Andrew Dean (joint with Luis Santiago)
note: Andrew Dean (joint with Luis Santiago), triples of real, complexified, and quaternionified Cuntz semigroups classify unital real AI algebras and their homomorphisms up to approximate unitary equivalence. Key computation: $\operatorname{Inv}(A)$ is the diagram $(\operatorname{Cu}(A),[1])\to(\operatorname{Cu}(A\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C),[1])\to(\operatorname{Cu}(A\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb H),[1])$; every morphism $\eta=(\eta_r,\eta_c,\eta_h):\operatorname{Inv}(A)\to\operatorname{Inv}(B)$ is realized by a unital $*$-homomorphism $\varphi:A\to B$ with $(\operatorname{Cu}(\varphi),\operatorname{Cu}(\varphi\otimes_{\mathbb R}\operatorname{id}_{\mathbb C}),\operatorname{Cu}(\varphi\otimes_{\mathbb R}\operatorname{id}_{\mathbb H}))=(\eta_r,\eta_c,\eta_h)$, and equality $\operatorname{Inv}(\varphi)=\operatorname{Inv}(\psi)$ implies $\varphi\sim_{\mathrm{a.u.}}\psi$.

title: Joachim Zacharias (joint with Joan Bosa
note: Joachim Zacharias (joint with Joan Bosa, Francesc Perera, and Jianchao Wu), almost elementary actions have $\mathcal Z$-stable crossed products and unify almost finite dynamics with $\mathcal Z$-stability of simple nuclear algebras. Key computation: a noncommutative tower is a c.p.c. order-zero map $\lambda:M_n\otimes C(S)\to A$ satisfying $\lambda(\,\cdot\,\otimes\delta_g)=\alpha_{gh^{-1}}\lambda(\,\cdot\,\otimes\delta_h)$; castles approximating finite sets with $1-\lambda(h)\precsim_G b$ and $\|h-g\cdot h\|<\varepsilon$ define almost elementariness, for which $\alpha:G\curvearrowright A\Rightarrow A\rtimes_\alpha G$ is almost elementary and hence $\mathcal Z$-stable, while for $A=C(X)$ and amenable $G$ the condition is equivalent to almost finiteness of $G\curvearrowright X$.

title: Marcelo Laca (joint with Camila F
note: Marcelo Laca (joint with Camila F. Sehnem), constructible right ideals and foundation-set relations give the full boundary quotient of a semigroup Toeplitz algebra and a criterion for its reduced quotient to be purely infinite simple. Key computation: for $P\subseteq G$, neutral words $\alpha$ produce projections $L_{\dot\alpha}=1_{K(\alpha)}$, and adjoining $\prod_{\beta\in F}(w_{\dot\alpha}-w_{\dot\beta})=0$ for every foundation cover $\bigcup_{\beta\in F}K(\beta)\subseteq K(\alpha)$ yields canonical isomorphisms $\mathcal C\rtimes_{\mathcal C P}P\cong C^*(w_p\mid\mathrm{(T1)-(T5)})\cong C(\partial\Omega_P)\rtimes_u G$; boundary topological freeness, equivalently condition $\mathrm{(BTF)}$, then makes $C(\partial\Omega_P)\rtimes_rG$ purely infinite simple, recovering this for $P=R\rtimes R^\times$ by explicitly choosing $s=(0,ac)$ or $s=(0,ac\bar x r)$ so that $psP\cap qsP=\varnothing$.

title: Gelu Popescu
note: Gelu Popescu, noncommutative Berezin kernels give a unique Wold decomposition and classify pure representations of the $C^*$-algebra of a noncommutative variety by multiplicity. Key computation: for $V_i=\pi(B_i)$ and $\Phi_{f,V}(Y)=\sum_{|\alpha|\ge1}a_\alpha V_\alpha YV_\alpha^*$, the projections $P_{\mathcal K_1}=\operatorname*{SOT-lim}_{s\to\infty}\Phi_{f,V}^s(I)$ and $P_{\mathcal K_0}=I-P_{\mathcal K_1}$ split $\mathcal K=\mathcal K_0\oplus\mathcal K_1$ into pure and Cuntz tuples; on $\mathcal K_0$, the constrained Berezin kernel is unitary and $V_i=K_{f,V,Q}^*(B_i\otimes I_{\mathcal D})K_{f,V,Q}$ with $\mathcal D=\operatorname{ran}(I-\Phi_{f,V})^m(I)^{1/2}$, so pure representations are unitarily equivalent exactly when $\dim\mathcal D$ agrees.

title: Leonel Robert
note: Leonel Robert, commutator subgroups of connected invertibles and unitaries in a unital $C^*$-algebra admit explicit exponential generators and strong simplicity properties. Key computation: the local Campbell--Baker--Hausdorff/Kashiwara--Vergne identities $e^xe^y=e^{x+y+[x,a]+[y,b]}$ and $e^{x+y}=(e^Re^xe^{-R})(e^Se^ye^{-S})$ show $e^{x+y}$ is commutator-equivalent to $e^xe^y$; consequently $D\mathrm{GL}_0(A)=\langle e^{[c,d]}:c,d\in A\rangle$ and $D\mathrm U_0(A)=\langle e^{i[x^*,x]}:x\in A\rangle$, and if $A$ has no one-dimensional representations then these groups are perfect, with $D\mathrm{GL}_0(A)$ generated by $1+x$ for $x^2=0$.

title: Camila F
note: Camila F. Sehnem (joint with Zahra Afsar, Marcelo Laca, and Jacqui Ramagge), the KMS$_\beta$ simplex of a Toeplitz noncommutative torus is classified by probability measures on a torus determined by the degeneracy of its zero-energy block. Key computation: for $r=(r_1,\ldots,r_k,0_d)$, every KMS state satisfies $\varphi(L_pL_xL_y^*L_q^*)=\delta_{p,q}e^{-\beta\langle p,r\rangle}\varphi(L_xL_y^*)$ and is obtained from a trace $\omega$ on $Q\mathcal T_r(\mathbb N^n,\sigma_\Theta)Q$ by $T_\beta(\omega)(X)=Z(\beta)^{-1}\sum_{l\in\mathbb N^k\times0_d}e^{-\beta\langle l,r\rangle}\omega(QL_l^*XL_lQ)$, where $Q=\prod_{j=1}^k(1-L_{e_j}L_{e_j}^*)$ and $Z(\beta)=\sum_pe^{-\beta\langle p,r\rangle}$; since traces on $A_{\Theta_d}$ are states on $Z(A_{\Theta_d})\cong C(\mathbb T^m)$, this gives $\operatorname{KMS}_\beta\cong\mathcal M_1(\mathbb T^m)$.

title: Sarah Reznikoff (joint with Jonathan Brown
note: Sarah Reznikoff (joint with Jonathan Brown, Adam Fuller, and David Pitts), regular ideals of a $C^*$-algebra are classified by invariant regular ideals of a regular subalgebra, and regular graph-algebra quotients preserve Condition (L). Key computation: for a regular inclusion $B\subseteq A$ with faithful invariant expectation $E:A\to B$ and regular ideal intersection property, $J\mapsto J\cap B$ and $K\mapsto J_K=\{a\in A:E(a^*a)\in K^{\perp\perp}\}$ are inverse Boolean-algebra isomorphisms between regular ideals of $A$ and invariant regular ideals of $B$; for graph algebras, $J=J^{\perp\perp}$ is equivalent to $p_w\in J\Longleftrightarrow(\forall v\in T(w))(\exists u\in T(v))\,p_u\in H(J)$, which forces every cycle of $E/J$ to retain an entrance and hence preserves Condition (L).

title: Paul Skoufranis
note: Paul Skoufranis, tracial inequalities completely characterize convex hulls of unitary orbits of self-adjoint elements in arbitrary unital $C^*$-algebras and extend to joint majorization of commuting tuples. Key computation: for self-adjoint $S,T\in A$, one has $S\in\overline{\operatorname{conv}}(\mathcal U(T))$ exactly when $\tau((S-\alpha)_+)\le\tau((T-\alpha)_+)$ and $\tau((-S-\alpha)_+)\le\tau((-T-\alpha)_+)$ for every lower-semicontinuous trace $\tau$ and $\alpha\in\mathbb R$; in $M_n$, this is equivalent to $\sum_{k=1}^ma_k\le\sum_{k=1}^mb_k$ for ordered eigenvalues (equality at $m=n$), to $a=Xb$ for a doubly stochastic $X$, and to a unital trace-preserving completely positive map $\Psi$ with $\Psi(T)=S$.

title: Dan Ursu (joint with Shirly Geffen)
note: Dan Ursu (joint with Shirly Geffen), simplicity of reduced crossed products by FC-hypercentral groups is characterized by the absence of a central corner on which a finite-conjugacy element acts inner with centralizer-invariant implementer. Key computation: for a minimal action $\alpha:G\curvearrowright A$ with $G$ FC-hypercentral, $A\rtimes_rG$ is not simple exactly when there exist $t\in\mathrm{FC}(G)\setminus\{e\}$, a nonzero $t$-invariant $p\in Z(I(A))$, and $u\in\mathcal U(I(A)p)$ such that $\alpha_t|_{I(A)p}=\operatorname{Ad}(u)$ and $\alpha_s(p)=p,\ \alpha_s(u)=u$ for every $s\in C_G(t)$; this refines proper outerness on the injective envelope and is equivalent, for separable $A$, to an intrinsic obstruction on an essential $t$-invariant ideal $J\triangleleft A$ with an implementing unitary in $M(J)$.

title: Matthew Kennedy
note: Matthew Kennedy, noncommutative Choquet theory classifies operator systems by compact matrix-convex state spaces and characterizes those arising from $C^*$-algebras as noncommutative Bauer simplices. Key computation: matrix convexity closes $K=\coprod_nK_n$ under $\sum_i\alpha_i^*x_i\alpha_i$ whenever $\sum_i\alpha_i^*\alpha_i=I$, and evaluation gives the dual equivalence $S\cong A(K)$; every $x\in K_n$ has a maximal representing nc state $\mu:C(K)\to M_n$ with $a(x)=\int_Ka\,d\lambda$ supported on $\partial K$, while uniqueness of this maximal state is equivalent to $A(K)^{**}$ being a von Neumann algebra and to $A(K)\otimes_cT=A(K)\otimes_{\max}T$ for every operator system $T$; adding closed $\partial K$ characterizes precisely nc state spaces of unital $C^*$-algebras.

title: Kenneth R
note: Kenneth R. Davidson, free semigroup algebras admit a Lebesgue--von Neumann--Wold decomposition and are uniformly hyperreflexive. Key computation: on Fock space $\mathcal F_n^2=\ell^2(\mathbb F_n^+)$ the left shifts satisfy $L_i^*L_j=\delta_{ij}I$ and $\sum_iL_iL_i^*=I-\xi_\varnothing\xi_\varnothing^*$, while $\mathcal L_n'=\mathcal R_n$ and every $A\in\mathcal L_n$ has Ces\`aro-summed Fourier expansion $A\sim\sum_wa_wL_w$; the structure projection $P$ determined by $\bigcap_{k\ge1}\mathcal S_0^k=\mathcal WP$ splits an arbitrary free semigroup algebra into von Neumann and type-$L$ corners, and Kennedy's wandering-vector theorem for absolutely continuous representations yields $\mathcal S\simeq\mathcal L^{(\alpha)}\oplus\mathcal S_a\oplus\mathcal S_{vN}\oplus\mathcal S_d$, with every free semigroup algebra hyperreflexive with constant at most $6$.

title: Michael Brannan
note: Michael Brannan, complete quantum graphs have no finite classical coloring but have quantum chromatic number exactly $n^2$, and their coloring algebras possess strongly solid noninjective factor representations. Key computation: the algebra $\mathcal A(\operatorname{Hom}(QK_n,K_{n^2}))$ is generated by $p_{ij}^{(a)}$ with $p_{ij}^{(a)}p_{kl}^{(a)}=\delta_{jk}n^{-1}p_{il}^{(a)}$, $\sum_jp_{ij}^{(a)}p_{jk}^{(b)}=\delta_{ab}p_{ik}^{(a)}$, $\sum_ip_{ii}^{(a)}=n^{-1}1$, and $\sum_ap_{ij}^{(a)}=\delta_{ij}1$; any unitary error basis $\{u_a\}_{a=1}^{n^2}\subset U(M_n)$ gives the representation $p_{ij}^{(a)}\mapsto n^{-1}u_a^*e_{ij}u_a$, while the quantum Hoffman bound supplies the reverse inequality, proving $\chi_q(QK_n)=n^2$ whereas $\chi_{\mathrm{loc}}(QK_n)=\infty$; for $n\ge3$ the same universal algebra has a faithful trace whose GNS algebra is a strongly solid noninjective $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor.

title: Ra\'ul E
note: Ra\'ul E. Curto (joint with In Sung Hwang and Woo Young Lee), Potapov's factorization theorem extends from matrices to rational two-sided inner operator-valued functions. Key computation: rationality is defined by the Hankel-kernel condition $\theta H^2(\mathbb T,E)\subseteq\ker H_{\Phi^*}$ for a finite Blaschke product $\theta$; if an inner $\Delta$ divides $\Theta=\theta I_E$, then $\Delta$ is a finite product of Blaschke--Potapov factors $b_\alpha P_M+(I_E-P_M)$, and the Beurling--Lax--Halmos identity $\ker H_{\Phi^*}=\Delta H^2$ yields the coprime factorization $\Phi=\Delta A^*$; consequently a two-sided inner $\Phi\in H^\infty(\mathbb T,B(E))$ is rational exactly when it is a finite Blaschke--Potapov product.

title: Ryan O'Loughlin
note: Ryan O'Loughlin, compact truncated Toeplitz operators on a model space have continuous inner-multiple symbols exactly under the same conditions that give bounded symbols for all bounded truncated Toeplitz operators. Key computation: for $K_I^2=H^2\ominus IH^2$ and $A_g^I f=P_I(gf)$, the projective product space $X=\{\sum_kx_ky_k:\sum_k\|x_k\|_2\|y_k\|_2<\infty\}$ satisfies $X^*=\mathcal T(I)$ and ${}^*X=\mathcal T_c(I)$; the maps $S:X\to zH^1\cap K_{I^2}^1$, $f\mapsto If$, ${}^*S:C(\mathbb T)/(F_{I^2}\cap C(\mathbb T))\to\mathcal T_c(I)$, $[f]\mapsto A_{If}^I$, and $S^*:L^\infty/Q\to\mathcal T(I)$ identify their images with compact operators having symbols in $I C(\mathbb T)$ and bounded-symbol operators, so duality gives $\mathcal T_c(I)=\{A_{Ih}^I:h\in C(\mathbb T)\}$ if and only if every bounded $A_g^I$ has a bounded symbol.

title: Alfons Van Daele
note: Alfons Van Daele, the polar decomposition of the antipode determines the modular structure of a locally compact quantum group and proves uniqueness of Haar weights. Key computation: regular representations satisfy $\Delta(x)=W^*(1\otimes x)W$ and $(\Delta\otimes\iota)W=W_{13}W_{23}$, while the closed antipode has $S((\iota\otimes\omega)W)=(\iota\otimes\omega)W^*$ and polar decomposition $S=R\tau_{-i/2}$; for two left Haar weights, $(K\otimes T_r)W_1=W_2^*(K\otimes T_r)$ implies $(1\otimes u_t)W_1(1\otimes u_t^*)=W_1$, hence $\Delta(u_t)=1\otimes u_t$ and $u_t$ is scalar, proving uniqueness up to scale; relative modular theory then produces the affiliated modular element $\delta$ with $\psi=\varphi(\delta^{1/2}\,\cdot\,\delta^{1/2})$, $\Delta(\delta)=\delta\otimes\delta$, and $\sigma_t'(x)=\delta^{it}\sigma_t(x)\delta^{-it}$.

title: Jingbo Xia
note: Jingbo Xia, the Drury--Arveson space is the universal dilation space for commuting row contractions and its multiplier norm gives the correct multivariable von Neumann inequality. Key computation: for a strict commuting row contraction $A=(A_1,\ldots,A_n)$, the identity $\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb Z_+^n}\frac{|\alpha|!}{\alpha!}A^\alpha(I-\sum_iA_iA_i^*)A^{*\alpha}=I$ makes $Zx=\sum_\alpha\frac{|\alpha|!}{\alpha!}(I-\sum_iA_iA_i^*)^{1/2}A^{*\alpha}x\,\zeta^\alpha$ an isometry into $H_n^2\otimes H$ satisfying $Zp(A^*)=(p(M_\zeta^*)\otimes I)Z$; hence $\|p(A)\|\leq\|p\|_{\operatorname{Mult}(H_n^2)}$, while for $\theta(\zeta)=\zeta_1\cdots\zeta_n$ one has $\|\theta^k\|_\infty=n^{-kn/2}$ but $\|\theta^k\|_{H_n^2}=((k!)^n/(nk)!)^{1/2}\asymp k^{(n-1)/4}n^{-kn/2}$, explicitly showing why the supremum norm cannot replace the multiplier norm for $n\ge2$.

title: Ilijas Farah
note: Ilijas Farah, set-theoretic saturation sharply classifies ultrapowers of separable $C^*$-algebras: CH makes all nonprincipal ultrapowers isomorphic, while failure of CH yields the maximal number of isomorphism types. Key computation: countably saturated elementarily equivalent structures $C,D$ of density $\aleph_1$ are written as continuous chains $C=\bigcup_{\alpha<\omega_1}C_\alpha$ and $D=\bigcup_{\alpha<\omega_1}D_\alpha$; a transfinite back-and-forth constructs compatible elementary embeddings whose unions are inverse isomorphisms, so under CH, $A^{\mathcal U}\cong A^{\mathcal V}$ commuting with the diagonal copy of every separable $A$ and $A'\cap A^{\mathcal U}\cong A'\cap A^{\mathcal V}$; conversely, if CH fails, every separable infinite-dimensional $A$ has $2^{2^{\aleph_0}}$ nonisomorphic ultrapowers and as many nonisomorphic relative commutants.

title: Guoliang Yu
note: Guoliang Yu, localization-algebra representatives refine higher indices to secondary rho invariants whose delocalized cyclic pairings recover Lott eta invariants. Key computation: partitions of unity on covers with mesh $<1/n$ localize $F=D(1+D^2)^{-1/2}$ to $F_n=\sum_k\sqrt{\phi_k^{(n)}}F\sqrt{\phi_k^{(n)}}$, and interpolation gives $\operatorname{propagation}(F_t)\to0$, defining $\operatorname{Index}_L(D)=[\exp(2\pi i(F_\bullet+1)/2)]\in K_1(C_L^*(\widetilde X)^G)$ with $e_*\operatorname{Index}_L(D)=\operatorname{Index}(D)$; when $D$ is invertible, splicing a trivialization to this path gives $\rho(D)\in K_*(C_{L,0}^*(\widetilde X)^G)$, and for a polynomial-growth conjugacy class $\langle h\rangle$, the explicit pairing $\tau_h(u)=(2\pi i)^{-1}\int_0^\infty\operatorname{tr}_h(\dot u(t)u(t)^{-1})dt$ satisfies $\tau_h(\rho(D))=\tfrac12\eta_{\langle h\rangle}(D)$.

title: Paolo Piazza (joint work with Hessel Posthuma
note: Paolo Piazza (joint work with Hessel Posthuma, Yanli Song, and Xiang Tang), cyclic cocycles on Harish--Chandra Schwartz algebras give delocalized Atiyah--Patodi--Singer formulas for cocompact proper actions of real reductive groups. Key computation: the Connes--Moscovici heat projector $V(D)$ has entries in $\mathcal A_G^\infty(Y)$ and defines $\operatorname{Ind}_\infty(D)$; extending the semisimple orbital integral $\tau_g(f)=\int_{G/Z_G(g)}f(xgx^{-1})d(xZ_G(g))$ and applying Melrose's defect formula ${}^b\!\operatorname{Tr}[R,T]=(i/2\pi)\int_{\mathbb R}\operatorname{Tr}(\partial_\lambda I(R,\lambda)I(T,\lambda))d\lambda$ produces a relative cyclic cocycle, whose pairing yields $\langle\operatorname{Ind}_\infty(D),\tau_g^Y\rangle=\int_{Y_0^g}c^g\operatorname{AS}_g(Y_0)-\tfrac12\eta_g(D_{\partial Y})$ with $\eta_g(D)=(1/\sqrt\pi)\int_0^\infty\tau_g(D e^{-tD^2})dt/\sqrt t$.

title: Masoud Khalkhali
note: Masoud Khalkhali, stable anti-Yetter--Drinfeld modules supply the coefficient objects that turn Hopf symmetries into cyclic modules and recover the Connes--Moscovici theory. Key computation: for a left $H$-module coalgebra $C$ and a right-left SAYD module $M$, the complex $C^n(C,M)=M\otimes_HC^{\otimes(n+1)}$ has cyclic operator $\tau_n(m\otimes c_0\otimes\cdots\otimes c_n)=m_{(0)}\otimes c_1\otimes\cdots\otimes c_n\otimes m_{(-1)}c_0$; the anti-Yetter--Drinfeld condition makes this operator descend through $\otimes_H$, and stability gives $\tau_n^{n+1}=\operatorname{id}$, hence a cocyclic module; modular pairs in involution $(\delta,\sigma)$ are exactly one-dimensional SAYD modules ${}^\sigma\mathbb C_\delta$, so taking $C=H$ recovers Connes--Moscovici Hopf cyclic cohomology and its characteristic map $\chi_\tau(h_1\otimes\cdots\otimes h_n)(a_0,\ldots,a_n)=\tau(a_0h_1(a_1)\cdots h_n(a_n))$.

title: Cong Xue
note: Cong Xue, the compactly supported relative cohomology of shtuka stacks is ind-smooth and carries an unramified product Weil action. Key computation: geometric Satake defines $\mathcal H^j_{N,I,W}=R^jp_!\mathcal F_{N,I,W}$ on $(X\setminus N)^I$; the partial Frobenius maps $F_{\{i\}}:\operatorname{Frob}_{\{i\}}^*\mathcal H^j_{N,I,W}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^j_{N,I,W}$ compose to total Frobenius, so Drinfeld's lemma gives a $\operatorname{Weil}(\eta)^I$-action on the generic fiber, while Eichler--Shimura relations, constancy on mixed loci $(\eta)^{I_1}\times(v)^{I_2}$, and creation--annihilation (Zorro) operators make every specialization map $(\mathcal H^j_{N,I,W})_y\to(\mathcal H^j_{N,I,W})_x$ an isomorphism; hence $\mathcal H^j_{N,I,W}$ is ind-smooth and the action factors through $\operatorname{Weil}(X\setminus N)^I$.

title: Clifton Cunningham (joint with Andrew Fiori and Qing Zhang)
note: Clifton Cunningham (joint with Andrew Fiori and Qing Zhang), microlocal geometry classifies the ABV packets of all six irreducible unipotent representations of $G_2(F)$ with subregular infinitesimal parameter and produces stable character combinations. Key computation: the parameter space is $X_{\mathrm{sub}}=(\widehat G_2\times V_{\mathrm{sub}})/H_{\mathrm{sub}}$ with $H_{\mathrm{sub}}\cong\mathrm{GL}_2$ and $V_{\mathrm{sub}}\cong\det^{-1}\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^3$, so $\operatorname{Per}_{\widehat G_2}(X_{\mathrm{sub}})\simeq\operatorname{Per}_{\mathrm{GL}_2}(\det^{-1}\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^3)$; the four binary-cubic orbits $C_0<C_1<C_2<C_3$ have microlocal groups $S_3,S_2,S_2,S_3$, and normalized microlocal vanishing cycles yield $\Pi^{\mathrm{ABV}}_{\phi_0}=\{\pi_0,\pi_1,\pi_3^\varepsilon\}$, $\Pi^{\mathrm{ABV}}_{\phi_1}=\{\pi_1,\pi_2,\pi_3^\varepsilon\}$, $\Pi^{\mathrm{ABV}}_{\phi_2}=\{\pi_2,\pi_3^\rho,\pi_3^\varepsilon\}$, and $\Pi^{\mathrm{ABV}}_{\phi_3}=\{\pi_3,\pi_3^\rho,\pi_3^\varepsilon\}$, with stable distributions including $\Theta_{\phi_3}=\Theta_{\pi_3}+2\Theta_{\pi_3^\rho}+\Theta_{\pi_3^\varepsilon}$.

title: Joachim Cuntz (joint with Guillermo Corti\~nas
note: Joachim Cuntz (joint with Guillermo Corti\~nas, Ralf Meyer, and Georg Tamme), the Feigin--Tsygan theorem identifies periodic cyclic homology of any finite-type commutative algebra in characteristic zero with the de Rham cohomology of a smooth formal presentation. Key computation: for a smooth surjection $P\twoheadrightarrow A=P/J$ and the $J$-adic completion $P_J=\varprojlim_nP/J^n$, flatness of $P_J$ over the Noetherian ring $P$ and two completed bar resolutions give a quasi-isomorphism $P_J\otimes_P(C(P),b)\to(C(P_J),b)$ and therefore $HH_*(P_J)\cong P_J\otimes_PHH_*(P)\cong P_J\otimes_P\Omega_P^*$ by HKR; under this identification Connes' $B$ becomes $d$, while nilpotent invariance gives $HP_*(A)\cong HP_*(P_J)$, hence $HP_*(A)\cong HP_*(P_J)\cong H^*_{\mathrm{dR}}(P_J)=H^*_{\mathrm{inf}}(A)$.

title: Victor Nistor
note: Victor Nistor, localization at conjugacy classes computes cyclic invariants of crossed products and reduces the periodic cyclic homology of a real algebraic group action to its maximal compact subgroup. Key computation: for a discrete action, the condition $\gamma_0\cdots\gamma_k\in\langle\gamma\rangle$ is preserved by Hochschild faces and cyclic permutation, giving $HH_k(A\rtimes\Gamma)\cong\bigoplus_{\langle\gamma\rangle}HH_k(A\rtimes\Gamma)_\gamma$ and $HH_*(A\rtimes\Gamma)_\gamma\cong HH_*(A\rtimes\Gamma)_{\mathfrak m_\gamma}$ for $\mathfrak m_\gamma=\{f\in C^\infty(\Gamma)^\Gamma:f(\gamma)=0\}$; for a connected real algebraic $G$ with maximal compact $K$ and $q=\dim(G/K)$, localization of the smooth convolution algebra then gives $HP_*(A\rtimes G)_{\mathfrak m}\cong HP_{*+q}(A\rtimes K)_{\mathfrak m}$, so every non-elliptic localization vanishes, while $HH_*(C^\infty(K))=C^\infty(K)^K$ and $HP_*(C^\infty(K))\cong C^\infty(K)^K\otimes\mathbb C[\sigma]$ with $|\sigma|=2$.

title: Katia Consani (joint with Alain Connes)
note: Katia Consani (joint with Alain Connes), Witt theory realizes the integral Bost--Connes algebra uniformly at finite and absolute arithmetic places. Key computation: $\mathcal A_{\mathbb Z}=\mathbb Z[\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z]\rtimes_\rho\mathbb N$ is generated by $e(\gamma),\widetilde\mu_n,\mu_n^*$ with $\rho_n(e(\gamma))=\sum_{n\gamma'=\gamma}e(\gamma')$ and $\mu_n^*\widetilde\mu_n=n$; for an embedding $\sigma:\overline{\mathbb F}_p^\times\hookrightarrow\mathbb C^\times$, the eigenvalue-divisor isomorphism $W_0(\overline{\mathbb F}_p)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbb Z[\overline{\mathbb F}_p^\times]$ intertwines $(F_n,V_n)$ with $(\sigma_n,\rho_n)$, yielding $\pi_\sigma(\mu_n^*)=F_n$ and $\pi_\sigma(\widetilde\mu_n)=V_n$ and extending continuously to $W(\overline{\mathbb F}_p)$; globally the Fourier-trace invariant gives $W_0(\mathbb S)\cong\mathbb Z[\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z]^{\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\times}}$ via $\widehat\tau(E,T)(n)=\operatorname{tr}(T^n|_{T^\infty(E(1_+))})$.

title: Deepak Kumar Pradhan (joint with K
note: Deepak Kumar Pradhan (joint with K. D. Deepak and Jaydeb Sarkar), partially isometric Toeplitz operators on the Hardy space of a polydisc are classified up to unitary equivalence as shifts, co-shifts, or direct sums of truncated shifts. Key computation: the Brown--Halmos relations $T_{z_i}^*TT_{z_i}=T$ force a partial-isometry symbol to depend on at most one of $z_i,\bar z_i$ for every $i$, and one obtains $T_\varphi=T_{\varphi_1}^*T_{\varphi_2}$ for inner $\varphi_1,\varphi_2\in H^\infty(\mathbb T^n)$ depending on disjoint variable sets; thus $D(T_\varphi)=\varphi_1H^2(\mathbb T^n)$, $R(T_\varphi)=\varphi_2H^2(\mathbb T^n)$, every $T_\varphi^m$ is again a partial isometry, and the Halmos--Wallen decomposition gives precisely the stated classification; moreover $[T_\varphi^*,T_\varphi]\ge0$ holds exactly when $\varphi$ is inner.

title: Orr Shalit
note: Orr Shalit, quotients of the Drury--Arveson multiplier algebra are classified by the complex geometry of their multiplier varieties. Key computation: for $k(z,w)=(1-\langle z,w\rangle)^{-1}$ and $H_V=\overline{\operatorname{span}}\{k_\lambda:\lambda\in V\}$, one has $\mathcal M_V=\operatorname{Mult}(H_V)\cong\mathcal M_d/J_V$; an isometric algebra isomorphism induces $\alpha=(\varphi(z_1),\ldots,\varphi(z_d))\in\operatorname{Aut}(\mathbb B_d)$ through $\varphi^*(\rho_\lambda)=\rho_{\alpha(\lambda)}$, while conversely $Uk_\lambda=c_\lambda k_{\alpha(\lambda)}$ implements the algebra isomorphism, proving $\mathcal M_V\cong_{\mathrm{c.i.}}\mathcal M_W$ exactly when an automorphism of $\mathbb B_d$ maps $W$ onto $V$; for homogeneous varieties, algebraic isomorphism, similarity, biholomorphic equivalence, and equivalence under an invertible linear map of $\mathbb C^d$ are all equivalent.

title: Branimir \v{C}a\'ci\'c
note:
Branimir \v{C}a'ci'c, quantum principal $U(1)$-bundles with connection are reconstructed from Hermitian line bimodules with connection, explicitly recovering the quantum Hopf fibration and its $q$-monopole. Key computation: the grading $\mathcal O_q(S^3)= igoplus_{m\in\mathbb Z}L_m$ has $L_m=\mathcal O_q(S^3)_m$ and $L_1$ a Hermitian line $\mathcal O_q(\mathbb{CP}^1)$-bimodule; with $\Omega_q^1(\mathbb{CP}^1)=L_{-2}\oplus L_2$, $\partial_+=\partial_{q^{1/2}EK}$, and $\partial_-=\partial_{q^{-1/2}FK}$, multiplication isomorphisms $\mu_{j,k}:L_j\otimes L_k\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{j+k}$ define $
abla_m^{(0)}=-i(\mu_{m,-2}^{-1}\partial_+,\mu_{m,2}^{-1}\partial_-)^T$, the unique left $\mathcal O_q(SU(2))$-covariant connection; its curvature and vertical deformation are $F_{[L_m,
abla_m]}=[m]_{q^{-2}}q^2\operatorname{vol}$ and $\kappa_{[L_m,
abla_m]}=q^{2m}$, and the differential Pimsner construction lifts $(L_1,
abla_1)$ uniquely to $(\mathcal O_q(S^3),\Omega_q(S^3),d_q,\Pi_q)$.

title: Robert T
note: Robert T. W. Martin, noncommutative rational functions in the free Hardy space are exactly rational Szeg\H{o} kernels with stable minimal realizations, leading to finite free Blaschke products and finitely correlated Clark measures. Key computation: a minimal descriptor realization $r(Z)=(I_n\otimes b^*)(I_n\otimes I_N-\sum_jZ_j\otimes A_j)^{-1}(I_n\otimes c)$ belongs to $H_d^2$ exactly when $\operatorname{spr}(A)<1$, equivalently when $A$ is jointly similar to a strict row contraction $W$ and $r=K\{W,y,v\}$, equivalently $\mathbb B_d^{\mathrm{nc}}\subseteq\operatorname{Dom}r$; rational inner--outer factorization stays rational, every rational inner is a finite product of irreducible free Blaschke factors, and a contractive $b$ is rational exactly when its Clark functional $\mu_b$ is finitely correlated, with $b$ inner exactly when the compressed tuple $T_{\mu_b}=(\Pi_{\mu_b}^*|_{H_{\mu_b}})^*$ is a finite row co-isometry.

title: Rapha\'el Ponge
note: Rapha\'el Ponge, measurable weak-trace-class operators are exactly Tauberian operators, giving a purely spectral formula for Connes' noncommutative integral and a semiclassical Weyl law for $L\log L$ potentials. Key computation: for $T\in\mathcal L_{1,\infty}$, $\tau(T)=[\{(\log N)^{-1}\sum_{k<N}\lambda_k(T)\}_N]\in\ell_\infty/c_0$ and every Dixmier trace is $\operatorname{Tr}_\omega=\omega\circ\tau$; independence of $\omega$ is equivalent to existence of $\lim_{N\to\infty}(\log N)^{-1}\sum_{k<N}\lambda_k(T)$, which equals $\mathop{\rlap{-}\!\int}T$; if $\int_M|V|\log(1+|V|)\,d\operatorname{vol}_g<\infty$, then $\Delta_g^{-n/4}V\Delta_g^{-n/4}\in\mathcal L_{1,\infty}$ and $\lim_{k\to\infty}k\lambda_k^\pm=c_n\int_MV_\pm\,d\operatorname{vol}_g$, hence $\mathop{\rlap{-}\!\int}\Delta_g^{-n/4}V\Delta_g^{-n/4}=c_n\int_MV\,d\operatorname{vol}_g$ and $\lim_{h\to0^+}h^nN^-(h^n\Delta_g+V)=c_n\int_MV_-\,d\operatorname{vol}_g$.

title: Steven Amelotte (joint with Ben Briggs)
note: Steven Amelotte (joint with Ben Briggs), componentwise almost-linear Stanley--Reisner resolutions classify a family of moment-angle manifolds as connected sums of sphere products. Key computation: for $S=\Bbbk[v_1,\ldots,v_m]$, the torus sweep operations assemble to $\delta=\sum_{U\subseteq[m]}v_U\otimes\delta_U$ on $S\otimes H^*(\mathcal Z_K)$, giving the minimal free resolution of $\Bbbk[K]$, while $H^*(\mathcal Z_K)\cong\operatorname{Tor}_S^*(\Bbbk[K],\Bbbk)$ and $H_i(\operatorname{lin}F_\bullet)=0$ for $1<i<\operatorname{projdim}\Bbbk[K]$ define the CAL condition; if $K$ is Gorenstein and CAL, then $\mathcal Z_K\simeq\mathbin{\#}$ sphere products and $\Omega\mathcal Z_K\simeq$ a product of loop spaces of spheres.

title: Reyer Sjamaar (joint with Yi Lin
note: Reyer Sjamaar (joint with Yi Lin, Yiannis Loizides, and Yanli Song), Euler-like Lie-algebroid retractions extend Darboux--Moser--Weinstein normal forms and Marsden--Weinstein reduction to symplectic Lie algebroids. Key computation: an Euler-like section along a clean intersection $j:N\hookrightarrow M$ produces a deformation retraction $\varrho:T[0,1]\times A\to A$ onto $j^!A$ and hence a homotopy equivalence $j_\sharp^*:\Omega_A^\bullet(U)\simeq\Omega_{j^!A}^\bullet(N)$; this supplies the Moser primitive giving $\varphi^*\omega_1=\omega_0$ near $N$, while for $N=\mu^{-1}(\mathcal O)$ the reduced form on $C\to Q=N/G$ is determined by $q_\sharp^*\omega_C=j_\sharp^*\omega-\operatorname{an}^*\mu_N^*\sigma_{\mathcal O}$.

title: Valentin Deaconu
note: Valentin Deaconu, pseudo-free self-similar groupoid actions produce ample groupoids whose Higman--Thompson groups are their topological full groups and satisfy Matui's AH exact sequence under pure infiniteness and minimality. Key computation: germs $[\alpha,g,\beta;\xi]$ form $\mathcal G(G,E)$ with cocycle $\rho([\alpha,g,\beta;\xi])=|\alpha|-|\beta|$ and kernel $\mathcal N(G,E)=\bigcup_k\mathcal N_k(G,E)$, where $\mathcal N_k(G,E)\cong(E^\infty\rtimes G)\times R_k$; the resulting long exact sequence with map $1-\rho_*$ computes $H_*(\mathcal G(G,E))$, and $V_E(G)\cong[[\mathcal G(G,E)]]$ fits into $H_0(\mathcal G)\otimes\mathbb Z_2\to[[\mathcal G]]_{\mathrm{ab}}\xrightarrow{I}H_1(\mathcal G)\to0$.

title: Asuman G\'uven Aksoy (joint with Yunied Puig)
note: Asuman G\'uven Aksoy (joint with Yunied Puig), backward weighted shifts characterize a nuclear operator ideal by an exact factorization theorem. Key computation: $T\in BN_{(w,p,q)}(X,Y)$ precisely when $T=RB_wS$ for $S:X\to\ell^{q'}$ and $R:\ell^p\to Y$, with $Sx=(a_i(x))_i$, $R((\nu_i))=\sum_i\nu_i y_i$, and $B_w=\sum_{i\ge2}w_i e_i^*\otimes e_{i-1}$; the representation $T=\sum_{i\ge2}w_i a_i\otimes y_{i-1}$ gives $\|T\|_{(w,p,q)}=\inf\|R\|\,\|B_w\|\,\|S\|$, and $1/s=1/p'+1/q'$ makes $(BN_{(w,p,q)},\|\cdot\|_{(w,p,q)})$ an $s$-Banach operator ideal.

title: Nathan Wagner (joint with Cody Stockdale)
note: Nathan Wagner (joint with Cody Stockdale), Berezin-transform boundary decay classifies compact Toeplitz operators on broad weighted Bergman spaces. Key computation: for $T_u f=P(uf)$ and normalized kernels $k_z(w)=(1-|z|^2)^{(n+1)/2}/(1-z\overline w)^{n+1}$, the Berezin transform $\widetilde T_u(z)=\langle T_uk_z,k_z\rangle$ satisfies $\widetilde T_u(z)\to0$ as $|z|\to1^-$ iff $T_u$ is compact on $A_\sigma^p$ when $\sigma\in B_p\cap RH_r$ and $\sigma^{1-p'}\in RH_r$; the underlying weighted Riesz--Kolmogorov criterion is $\lim_{r\to1^-}\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\int_{r\mathbb B_n^c}|f|^p\sigma\,dV=0$, and sparse domination $|T_uf(z)|\lesssim\sum_{K\in\mathcal D}\langle|uf|\rangle_{\widehat K}\chi_{\widehat K}(z)$ yields boundedness for the larger $uB_p$ classes.

title: Pascal Lef\`evre (joint with Tonie Far\`es)
note: Pascal Lef\`evre (joint with Tonie Far\`es), an explicit integral condition completely classifies absolutely summing composition operators between Bloch-type spaces and produces nuclear inner-symbol examples. Key computation: for $\varphi:\mathbb D\to\mathbb D$, $C_\varphi:\mathcal B^\mu\to\mathcal B^\beta$ is $p$-summing exactly when $\int_{\mathbb D}\sup_{z\in\mathbb D}\left(\frac{(1-|w|^2)^2}{|1-\overline w\varphi(z)|^2}\right)^p\left(\frac{(1-|z|^2)^\beta|\varphi'(z)|}{|1-\overline w\varphi(z)|^\mu}\right)^p\frac{dA(w)}{(1-|w|^2)^2}<\infty$; for lens maps $\varphi_\theta$, this gives $C_{\varphi_\theta}$ $p$-summing when $p>\theta/((\beta-1)(1-\theta))$ and nuclear when $\theta<1-1/\beta$, while suitable Blaschke products yield nuclear $C_\varphi$ on $\mathcal B^\beta$ for $\beta\ge1$.

title: Hugo J
note: Hugo J. Woerdeman, positive structured completions of multilevel Toeplitz matrices classify stable multivariable autoregressive filters. Key computation: in two variables, Fourier data $c_k=\overline{c_{-k}}$ on $\mathbf n=\{0,\ldots,n_1\}\times\{0,\ldots,n_2\}$ come from a stable spectral density $|p(z_1,z_2)|^{-2}$ exactly when the missing coefficients can be chosen so that $T_{\mathbf n}=(c_{k-\ell})_{k,\ell\in\mathbf n}>0$ and $\operatorname{rank}(c_{k-\ell})_{k\in\{1,\ldots,n_1\}\times\{0,\ldots,n_2\},\,\ell\in\{0,\ldots,n_1\}\times\{1,\ldots,n_2\}}=n_1n_2$; for $c_{00}=1$ and $c_{01}=c_{10}=c_{11}=0.9$, the completion is explicitly $c_{1,-1}=0.81$, making the Toeplitz matrix positive definite and producing the stable filter.

title: Herv\'e Queff\'elec (joint with Pascal Lef\`evre
note: Herv\'e Queff\'elec (joint with Pascal Lef\`evre, Daniel Li, and Luis Rodr\'iguez-Piazza), conditional multipliers of admissible weighted Hardy spaces classify symbols by strict range contraction and finite Blaschke products. Key computation: for $H=H^2(\beta)$ and $M(H,\varphi)=\{w:w(f\circ\varphi)\in H\ \forall f\in H\}$, one has $M(H^2,\varphi)\subseteq M(H,\varphi)$ and the sharp equivalences $M(H,\varphi)=H\Longleftrightarrow\|\varphi\|_\infty<1$ and $M(H,\varphi)=H^\infty\Longleftrightarrow\varphi$ is a finite Blaschke product; for $H^2$, the kernel estimate $\|K_a\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\sqrt{(1+|\varphi(a)|)/(1-|\varphi(a)|)}(1-|a|^2)^{-1/2}$ turns $M(H^2,\varphi)=H^\infty$ into $\sup_a(1-|\varphi(a)|)/(1-|a|)<\infty$, which is precisely the finite-Blaschke condition.

title: P
note: P. Muthukumar, a Schur-class divisibility condition classifies exactly which Beurling subspaces are invariant under a composition operator. Key computation: for inner $\theta$ and analytic $\varphi:\mathbb D\to\mathbb D$, the conditions $C_\varphi(\theta H^2)\subseteq\theta H^2$ and $(\theta\circ\varphi)/\theta\in\mathcal S(\mathbb D)$ are equivalent; Douglas range inclusion rewrites this as $C_\varphi M_\theta=M_\theta X$, and evaluation of $X^*M_\theta^*=M_\theta^*C_\varphi^*$ on $K_w(z)=(1-\overline wz)^{-1}$ yields $X^*(\overline{\theta(w)}K_w)=\overline{\theta(\varphi(w))}K_{\varphi(w)}$, giving an equivalent bounded-kernel criterion and, for Blaschke $B$, the zero-multiplicity test $\operatorname{mult}_B(w)\le\operatorname{mult}_{B\circ\varphi}(w)$.

title: Dragan Vukoti\'c (joint work with Alexandru Aleman and Aristomenis Siskakis)
note: Dragan Vukoti\'c (joint work with Alexandru Aleman and Aristomenis Siskakis), the conformal-invariance index of an analytic Banach space determines the complete spectrum of its Hilbert matrix operator. Key computation: the weighted automorphisms $W_a^{1/2}f=(\varphi_a')^{1/2}(f\circ\varphi_a)$ have generator $Df(z)=(1-z^2)f'(z)-zf(z)$ with $\sigma(D)=S_\alpha=\{\lambda:|\operatorname{Re}\lambda|\le|1-2\alpha|\}$, and $Kf(z)=\int_{-1}^1f(r)/(1-rz)\,dr=\int_{-1}^1W_a^{1/2}f(z)\,da/\sqrt{1-a^2}$; spectral mapping gives $\sigma(H)=\sigma(K)=\{0\}\cup\{\pi/\cos(\pi\lambda/2):\lambda\in S_\alpha\}$ and $r(H)=\pi/\cos(\pi|\alpha-1/2|)$, recovering $\sigma(H)=[0,\pi]$ when $\alpha=1/2$.

title: Francesco Fournier-Facio (joint with Bharatram Rangarajan)
note: Francesco Fournier-Facio (joint with Bharatram Rangarajan), every lamplighter $\Gamma\wr\mathbb Z$ is Ulam stable with a linear estimate, which implies the same for Thompson's groups $F',F,T$ and embeds every countable group in a three-generated linearly Ulam-stable group. Key computation: an asymptotic homomorphism $\varphi_n:\Gamma\to U(k_n)$ defines $W=\prod_{n\to\omega}\mathfrak u(k_n)$ and an Ulam class $\alpha_\varphi\in H_a^2(\Gamma,W)$, with $\alpha_\varphi=0$ equivalent to a defect-diminishing correction $\operatorname{dist}(\varphi_n,\psi_n)=O_\omega(\operatorname{def}(\varphi_n))$ and $\operatorname{def}(\psi_n)=o_\omega(\operatorname{def}(\varphi_n))$; the highly ergodic Zimmer-amenable model for $\Gamma\wr\mathbb Z$ makes the relevant invariant cochain complex alternate $\operatorname{id}$ and $0$, killing every Ulam class, while the coamenable inclusion $F[a,b]\cong F< F'$ injects restriction on $H_a^2$ and transfers the vanishing to $F',F,T$.

title: Stephen S
note: Stephen S. Kudla, the numerical ring of special cycles on an orthogonal Shimura variety is determined by Fourier coefficients of pullbacks of Hilbert--Siegel Eisenstein series and depends only on the finite quadratic space. Key computation: the theta-form identity $[\theta(g_\tau';\varphi)]=\phi_n(\tau;\varphi)=\sum_{T\ge0}Z(T,\varphi)q^T$ and wedge compatibility $\varphi_\infty^{(n_1+n_2)}=\varphi_\infty^{(n_1)}\wedge\varphi_\infty^{(n_2)}$, followed by Siegel--Weil, give $\langle z(T_1,\varphi_1),z(T_2,\varphi_2)\rangle=A(T_1,T_2;\lambda_{V_f}(\varphi_1\otimes\varphi_2))$ for $n_1+n_2=m$ and $\langle z(T_1,\varphi_1)z(T_2,\varphi_2),z(T_3,\varphi_3)\rangle=A(T_1,T_2,T_3;\lambda_{V_f}(\varphi_1\otimes\varphi_2\otimes\varphi_3))$ for $n_1+n_2+n_3=m$; nondegeneracy determines multiplication, and matching Schwartz functions for $V(\mathbb A_f)\simeq V'(\mathbb A_f)$ yield an isometric graded-ring isomorphism $SC^\bullet(V)\simeq SC^\bullet(V')$.

title: Iskander A
note: Iskander A. Taimanov, the generalized Kummer resolution gives an explicit intersection-ring classification for a simply connected Joyce $G_2$-manifold and shows that it has no nontrivial Massey products. Key computation: for the commuting involutions $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ on $T^7$ with $\Gamma\cong(\mathbb Z/2)^3$, one computes $b_1(T^7/\Gamma)=b_2(T^7/\Gamma)=0$ and $b_3(T^7/\Gamma)=b_4(T^7/\Gamma)=7$; resolving the twelve singular $T^3\times(D/\{\pm1\})$ strata adds classes giving $b_2(M)=12$ and $b_3(M)=43$, and the nonzero products in the homology intersection ring are $c_{\delta i}\cap c'_{\delta i}=-2$, $c_{\delta ij}\cap c'_{\delta ij}=-2$, $t_\delta\cap t'_\delta=4$, $t_i\cap t'_i=8$, $c'_{\delta i}\cap c'_{\delta i}=-2t_\delta$, and $t'_\delta\cap c'_{\delta i}=4c_{\delta i}$, which by Poincar\'e duality determines $H^*(M;\mathbb Q)$.

title: Herbert Gangl
note: Herbert Gangl, explicit polylogarithmic functional equations realize Zagier's polylogarithm conjecture through weight four and construct higher-weight analogues of the decisive motivic relation. Key computation: Bloch's map $\delta_2^F:\mathbb Z[F]\to\bigwedge^2F^\times$, $[x]\mapsto x\wedge(1-x)$, together with the exact sequence $0\to T(F)\to K_3(F)/K_3^M(F)\to B_2(F)\to0$, turns the single-valued dilogarithm into the regulator formula $\pi^{r_2}\zeta_F^*(-1)=q\det(\mathcal L_2(\xi_i^\sigma))_{i,\sigma}$; at weight four an explicit 122-term reduction $I_{3,1}(z,V(x,y))\equiv\sum_{i=1}^{122}c_i\operatorname{Li}_4(f_i(x,y,z))$ modulo lower-weight products supplies the $Q_4$ relation used by Goncharov--Rudenko to prove the conjecture for $m=4$, while the explicit quadruple ratio is a 368-orbit combination on eight points in $\mathbb P^3$ representing a nonzero class in $H^7(GL_4(\mathbb C),\mathbb R)$.

title: Jongbaek Song (joint with Xin Fu and Tseleung So)
note: Jongbaek Song (joint with Xin Fu and Tseleung So), the fan vectors of a compact toric surface determine its integral cohomology ring through an explicit cup-product matrix. Key computation: for rays $(-1,0),(0,-1),(a_1,b_1),\ldots,(a_n,b_n)$, a cellular cofibration $S^3\to\bigvee_{i=1}^nS_i^2\to X_\Sigma$ yields bases $H^2(X_\Sigma;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z\langle u_1,\ldots,u_n\rangle$ and $H^4(X_\Sigma;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z\langle v\rangle$; the weighted Stanley--Reisner model and the morphisms $X_\Sigma\to\mathbb{CP}_{1,a_i,b_i}^2$ send $[a_ib_ix_1]$ to $\sum_{k<i}a_kb_i y_k+a_ib_i y_i+\sum_{k>i}a_ib_k y_k$ and $[x_2x_3]$ to $[y_{n+1}y_{n+2}]$, so $u_i\smile u_j=a_{\min(i,j)}b_{\max(i,j)}v$ and $M(X_\Sigma)_{ij}=a_{\min(i,j)}b_{\max(i,j)}$.

title: Lisa Jeffrey (joint with Nan-Kuo Ho
note: Lisa Jeffrey (joint with Nan-Kuo Ho, Paul Selick, and Eugene Xia), Mayer--Vietoris decompositions compute the integral cohomology ring of the genus-two $SU(2)$ character variety with puncture monodromy $-I$ and identify its connected-sum type. Key computation: with $M=\mu^{-1}(-I)$ and $A=M/SU(2)$, the commutator trace stratification gives $A\simeq T\cup_{\mathbb{RP}^3\times S^2}T$, where $T=\{(g,h):[g,h]=I\}\simeq S^3\vee S^3\vee S^2\vee\Sigma^2\mathbb{RP}^2$; the prequantum bundle Mayer--Vietoris sequence $0\to\mathbb Z/2\to H^4(L;\mathbb Z)\to\mathbb Z/2\to0$ and $H^4(L;\mathbb Z/2)=\mathbb Z/2$ force $H^4(L;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z/4$, and yield $H^*(A)=\langle1,x,s_1,s_2,s_3,s_4,y,z\rangle$ with $|x|=2$, $|s_i|=3$, $|y|=4$, $|z|=6$, $x^2=4y$, and $xy=s_1s_3=s_2s_4=z$; Wall's theorem then gives $A\cong A^0\#(S^3\times S^3)\#(S^3\times S^3)$.

title: Ron Donagi
note: Ron Donagi, supermoduli is non-split and non-projected in genus at least five, while the super Mumford isomorphism constructs natural measures that extend across the vanishing-theta-null locus and, with Ramond punctures, across codimension at least two. Key computation: a supermanifold $S=(M,\mathcal O_S)$ has splitting obstruction $\omega\in H^1(M,T_M\otimes\bigwedge^2V^*)$, appearing as the third component of its super Atiyah class alongside the Atiyah classes of $T_+S$ and $T_-S$; for $\mathfrak M_g$, $\dim\mathfrak M_g=(3g-3\mid2g-2)$ with $T_+|_{[S]}=H^1(T_M)$ and $T_-|_{[S]}=H^1(T_M^{1/2})$, and restricting $\omega$ to a lifted family of odd-branched covers gives $\omega\ne0$ for $g\ge5$; the identity $\mathcal L_{3/2}\simeq\mathcal L_{1/2}^{5}$ defines the superstring measure, and a codimension-$\ge2$ Hartogs extension gives a natural measure on $\mathfrak M_{g,0,r}$ for $r\ge2$ Ramond punctures.

title: Meng Fai Lim
note: Meng Fai Lim, the growth of \'etale wild kernels in multi-false-Tate towers is controlled by an Iwasawa-module rank, and its smaller-order growth is equivalent to the noncommutative Greenberg conjecture. Key computation: Poitou--Tate duality identifies $R_i(F)=WK_{2i}^{\mathrm{\acute et}}(F)^\vee$ with the kernel of $H^1(G_S(F),\mathbb Q_p/\mathbb Z_p(-i))\to\bigoplus_{v\in S}H^1(F_v,\mathbb Q_p/\mathbb Z_p(-i))$; Hochschild--Serre gives $\ker h_n=H^1(G_n,\mathbb Q_p/\mathbb Z_p(-i)(F_\infty))$ and $\operatorname{coker}h_n\subseteq H^2(G_n,\mathbb Q_p/\mathbb Z_p(-i)(F_\infty))$, yielding $e(R_i(F_\infty)^{G_n})-e(R_i(F_n))=O(np^{(d-2)n})$; if the cyclotomic $\mu$-conjecture holds, then $e(WK_{2i}^{\mathrm{\acute et}}(F_n))=\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Z_p[[H]]}Y_i(F_\infty)\,np^{(d-1)n}+O(p^{(d-1)n})$, and vanishing of this rank is equivalent to $\operatorname{Gal}(K(F_\infty)/F_\infty)$ being pseudo-null.

title: Soumen Sarkar
note: Soumen Sarkar, weighted Grassmann orbifolds have torsion-free integral cohomology concentrated in even degrees, and their integral equivariant cohomology is completely encoded by an orbifold GKM graph. Key computation: for $W=(w_1,\ldots,w_n)$ and $a\ge1$, $WGr(d,n)=M_d(n,d;\mathbb C)/{\sim_W}$ with $(a_1,\ldots,a_n)^t\sim_W(t^{w_1}a_1,\ldots,t^{w_n}a_n)^tT$ whenever $t^a=\det T$; its finite-quotient strata satisfy that $H_j(U(L)/G;\mathbb Z)$ has no $p$-torsion for $p\nmid|G|$, producing a torsion-free even-dimensional cellular filtration; each $WGr(d,n)$ is consequently a GKM orbifold and $H_{T^n}^*(WGr(d,n);\mathbb Z)\cong\{f:V(\Gamma)\to H^*(BT^n;\mathbb Z)\mid r_e\alpha(e)\text{ divides }f(s(e))-f(t(e))\}=H_{T^n}^*(\Gamma,\alpha,\theta)$.

title: Payman Eskandari (joint with Kumar Murty)
note: Payman Eskandari (joint with Kumar Murty), the Ceresa cycle of every Fermat curve $F(p)$ of prime degree $p>7$ has infinite order modulo rational equivalence, for every base point. Key computation: quadratic iterated integrals give $E_e^\infty\in\operatorname{Ext}((H^1)^{\otimes3},\mathbb Q(-1))$, and for a correspondence $Z$ the Darmon--Rotger--Sols formula is $\xi_Z^{-1}(E_e^\infty)=(\int_\Delta\xi_Z)(\infty-e)-P_Z$; taking $Z$ as the graph of $(x,y,z)\mapsto(-y,z,x)$ on $F(p)$ gives fixed points $Q=(\eta,\eta^{-1},1)$ and $\bar Q=(\eta^{-1},\eta,1)$ and hence $P_Z=Q+\bar Q-2e$, which Gross--Rohrlich proves has infinite order while $\infty-e$ is torsion; thus $E_e^\infty\ne0$, its $H^1\otimes\xi_\Delta$ component $-2g\infty+2e+K$ is torsion, and Harris--Pulte identifies the remaining component with $\tfrac12AJ(F(p)_e-F(p)_e^-)$, forcing the Abel--Jacobi image, and therefore the Ceresa cycle, to be nonzero.

title: Avi Zeff
note: Avi Zeff, prismatic cohomology of quasiregular semiperfectoid rings is computed in degree zero and its Nygaard completion recovers the even homotopy of $\mathrm{THH}$, $\mathrm{TC}^-$, and $\mathrm{TP}$. Key computation: the initial prism $(\Delta_R^{\mathrm{init}},(d))$ gives $\Delta_{R/A}=\Delta_R=\Delta_R^{\mathrm{init}}$ and $N^{\ge i}\Delta_R=\varphi^{-1}(d^i\Delta_R)$; after Nygaard completion, $\pi_{2*}\mathrm{THH}(R)=N^*\widehat\Delta_R\{*\}$, $\pi_{2*}\mathrm{TC}^-(R)=N^{\ge *}\widehat\Delta_R\{*\}$, and $\pi_{2*}\mathrm{TP}(R)=\widehat\Delta_R\{*\}$, with all odd homotopy groups vanishing.

title: David Mart\'inez-Carpena (with Carles Casacuberta and Javier J
note: David Mart\'inez-Carpena (with Carles Casacuberta and Javier J. Guti\'errez), presentable $\infty$-categories are exactly the categories of models of limit $\infty$-sketches. Key computation: for a limit $\infty$-sketch $\Sigma=(A,L)$, $\operatorname{Mod}(\Sigma)=\{F:A\to\mathcal S\mid F(\alpha)\text{ is limiting for every }\alpha\in L\}$ is presentable, and conversely every presentable $\infty$-category $\mathcal C$ admits a normal $\Sigma$ with $\mathcal C\simeq\operatorname{Mod}(\Sigma)$; concretely, the cones $\alpha_n$ on $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ impose $F_n\simeq F_1\times_{F_0}\cdots\times_{F_0}F_1$, so their models are Segal spaces, while adjoining the univalence cone produces complete Segal spaces.

title: Andr\'e Joyal
note: Andr\'e Joyal, the free bicompletion of a locally small category is characterized intrinsically by softness together with atomic and co-atomic generators. Key computation: softness requires the canonical square from $\operatorname*{colim}_I\operatorname*{lim}_J\mathcal E(A_i,B_j)$ to $\mathcal E(\operatorname*{lim}_I A_i,\operatorname*{colim}_J B_j)$ to be a pushout; hence every $f:\prod_{i\in I}A_i\to\coprod_{j\in J}B_j$ factors through some projection $\prod_iA_i\to A_i$, some inclusion $B_j\to\coprod_jB_j$, or both, and $\eta:K\to\Lambda(K)$ is the free bicompletion precisely when $\Lambda(K)$ is bicomplete and soft, $\eta$ is fully faithful and generating, and each $\eta(A)$ is atomic and co-atomic.

title: Nathanael Arkor and Dylan McDermott
note: Nathanael Arkor and Dylan McDermott, the algebras of any relative monad rooted at a dense functor are reconstructed as a pullback along the corresponding nerve, subsuming standard nerve theorems. Key computation: for $j:A\to E$ dense and a $j$-relative monad $T$ with $\operatorname{Kl}(T)(x,y)=E(jx,ty)$, the square $\operatorname{Alg}(T)\to\widehat{\operatorname{Kl}(T)}$ over $E\xrightarrow{n_j}\widehat A$, where $n_j(e)=E(j-,e)$, is a pullback in $\operatorname{Cat}$; thus $\operatorname{Kl}(T)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Alg}(T)$ is dense, and for an ordinary monad the analogous square is a pullback exactly when $T$ is $j$-ary, recovering algebraic theories and the Segal-nerve classification of categories.

title: Joanna Ko
note: Joanna Ko, enhanced simplicial categories of $(\infty,1)$-categories with specified limits and lax morphisms admit the higher limit constructions needed for Eilenberg--Moore objects. Key computation: $J\text{-}\operatorname{Lim}$ admits rigged $n$-inserters, so in particular comma objects whose projections preserve and jointly reflect $J$-shaped limits; since a loose homotopy-coherent monad's Eilenberg--Moore object is assembled from simplicial powers, rigged $n$-inserters, and limits of countable chains of tight isofibrations, $\operatorname{Lali}(\mathcal K)$ admits such Eilenberg--Moore objects and its forgetful functor is exact and detects exactness, recovering that $U:T\text{-}\operatorname{Alg}\to A$ lifts $J$-limits even when $T$ does not preserve them.

title: Seerp Roald Koudenburg
note: Seerp Roald Koudenburg, formal Day convolution lifts Yoneda morphisms and yields a monoidal double Grothendieck correspondence. Key computation: a lax $T$-algebra $(A,\alpha)$ and Yoneda morphism $y:A\to\widehat A$ lift, when the pointwise weak composite $\alpha_*\odot Ty_*$ exists, to a lax $T$-algebra structure on $\widehat A$ for which $y$ is pseudo-$T$, giving $\widehat A(y,-):(\operatorname{Lax}\text{-}T\text{-}\operatorname{Mor}(B,\widehat A))\simeq(T\text{-}\operatorname{Mor}(A,B))$; for $y:A\to\operatorname{Set}^{A^{\mathrm{op}}}$ this constructs Day convolution, while for $Y:1\to\operatorname{Span}(\operatorname{Cat})$ it identifies lax monoidal lax double functors $G:(B,\otimes)\to(\operatorname{Span}(\operatorname{Cat}),\times)$ with lax monoidal double split opfibrations $\int G\to B$.

title: Fosco Loregian
note: Fosco Loregian, bicategorical Moore machines are models of a finite weighted-limit sketch and their universal machine is computed by a right Kan extension. Key computation: classical machines arise from pullbacks $\operatorname{Mly}(F,B)=\operatorname{Alg}(F)\times_K(F/B)$ and $\operatorname{Mre}(F,B)=\operatorname{Alg}(F)\times_K(K/B)$; in a bicategory, a fixed-input/output biMoore machine fills the $2$-cells $\delta:e\circ i\Rightarrow e$ and $\sigma:e\Rightarrow o$, and its terminal object is $\operatorname{Ran}_{i^\sharp}(o)$ along the free monad $i^\sharp:A\to A$, recovering $[A^*,B]$ in the one-object closed-monoidal case and extending the construction to $(T,V)$-profunctors.

title: Arne Mertens (joint with Wendy Lowen)
note: Arne Mertens (joint with Wendy Lowen), necklace-parametrized templicial objects define quasi-categories enriched in a non-cartesian monoidal category and explicitly compute left adjoints to enriched nerve functors. Key computation: the nerve has $N_V(C)_n=C_1\otimes_{C_0}\cdots\otimes_{C_0}C_1$ and comultiplications $\mu_{k,l}:X_{k+l}\to X_k\otimes_{X_0}X_l$ indexed by inclusions $\Delta^k\vee\Delta^l\hookrightarrow\Delta^{k+l}$; if $\pi D\simeq\operatorname{Lan}_\iota D'$, then $\pi(L_DX(a,b))\simeq\coprod_{T\in\operatorname{Nec}}F(X_T^{\mathrm{nd}}(a,b))\otimes D'(T)$, yielding for Lurie's dg nerve $L_{\mathrm{dg}}(X)_n(a,b)\simeq\bigoplus_{\dim T=n}k\!\cdot\!X_T^{\mathrm{nd}}(a,b)$.

title: Samarpita Ray (joint with Abhishek Banerjee and Mamta Balodi)
note: Samarpita Ray (joint with Abhishek Banerjee and Mamta Balodi), representations of coalgebras have Grothendieck categories of cis- and trans-comodules, with cartesian subcategories serving as coalgebraic analogues of quasi-coherent sheaves. Key computation: for $C:X\to\operatorname{Coalg}$ with right-semiperfect values, a map $V\to M_x$ from a finite-dimensional projective generates $N_y=\operatorname{Im}(\bigoplus_{\beta:x\to y}\beta_*V\to M_y)$ with $|N|\le\kappa=\sup\{\aleph_0,|\operatorname{Mor}X|,|K|\}$, and every $M$ is a sum of such $N$, proving $\operatorname{Com}^{\mathrm{cs}}\!\text{-}C$ is Grothendieck; if $C$ is quasi-finite then $\alpha_!=H_{C_y}(C_x,-)\dashv\alpha^*$ gives the corresponding Grothendieck classification for $\operatorname{Com}^{\mathrm{tr}}\!\text{-}C$, while semiperfect $C$ makes $\operatorname{Com}^{\mathrm{cs}}\!\text{-}C$ a hereditary torsion class in $C^*\text{-}\operatorname{Mod}^{\mathrm{tr}}$.

title: Brais Ramos P\'erez
note: Brais Ramos P\'erez, modules over invertible Hopf-algebra $1$-cocycles are equivalent to modules over the associated Hopf braces. Key computation: an invertible $1$-cocycle is a coalgebra isomorphism $\pi:A\to H$ satisfying $\pi\circ\mu_A=\mu_H\circ(\pi\otimes\varphi_H)\circ(\delta_A\otimes\pi)$; it produces the brace $H_\pi=Q(\pi,\varphi_H)$, and the functor $H_\pi:(\pi,\varphi_H)\text{-}\operatorname{Mod}\to H_\pi\text{-}\operatorname{Mod}$ sends $(M,N,\varphi_M,\phi_M,\varphi_N,\gamma)$ to $(M,\phi_M,\gamma\circ\varphi_N\circ(\pi^{-1}\otimes\gamma^{-1}))$, with inverse $M_{(\pi,\operatorname{id}_H)}\circ G_{H_\pi}$, so the composites are $\operatorname{id}_{H_\pi\text{-}\operatorname{Mod}}$ and naturally isomorphic to $\operatorname{id}_{(\pi,\varphi_H)\text{-}\operatorname{Mod}}$.

title: Ivan Limonchenko (joint with Rade \v{Z}ivaljevi\'c and Matvey Sergeev)
note: Ivan Limonchenko (joint with Rade \v{Z}ivaljevi\'c and Matvey Sergeev), flag Bier spheres are classified by four families of simple polytopes, and every Bier sphere canonically determines smooth moment-angle and toric manifolds. Key computation: every flag $\operatorname{Bier}(K)$ is the nerve of $I^n$, $I^n\times Q_5$, $I^n\times Q_6$, or $I^n\times P_4$; moreover $s_{\mathbb R}(\operatorname{Bier}(K))=s(\operatorname{Bier}(K))=m+1$, and the cones $C(\sigma,\tau)=\mathbb R_{\ge0}\langle-e_p,e_q\mid p\in\sigma,\ q'\in\tau\rangle$ form a complete regular fan $\Sigma(K)\subset\mathbb R^{m-1}$, producing the smooth manifolds $Z_{\operatorname{Bier}(K)}^{3m-1}$ and $X_{\Sigma(K)}^{2(m-1)}$.

title: Daisuke Kishimoto (joint with Kouyemon Iriye)
note: Daisuke Kishimoto (joint with Kouyemon Iriye), a triangulation of an $\mathbb F$-orientable manifold is $\mathbb F$-Golod if and only if it is $\mathbb F$-tight. Key computation: the dga $C^*(K)$ with $C^p(K)=\bigoplus_{\varnothing\ne I\subset[m]}\widetilde C^{p-|I|-1}(K_I)$ is homotopy equivalent to the Koszul complex of $\mathbb F[K]$; tightness lifts cocycles from $\widetilde C^*(K_I)$ to $\widetilde C^*(K)$, and higher prism operators $P_H$ obey $\partial P_H+(-1)^{q-1}P_H\partial=\sum_{i=0}^q(-1)^iP_{H\circ(1\otimes d^i)}$, furnishing the higher homotopies that kill every product and Massey product in $H^*(C^*(K))\cong\operatorname{Tor}^S(\mathbb F[K],\mathbb F)$.

title: Alexandru Suciu (joint work with Aprodu
note: Alexandru Suciu (joint work with Aprodu, Farkas, Raicu, and Sama), the support resonance schemes of every simplicial complex are reduced coordinate-subspace arrangements, and their Koszul modules are computed from induced-subcomplex cohomology. Key computation: for $\Delta$ on $V=[n]$, $\mathcal R^i(\Delta)=\bigcup_{W\subseteq V\,\mathrm{maximal},\,\widetilde H^{i-1}(\Delta_W;k)\ne0}k^W$ is the irreducible-component decomposition of the reduced support scheme, while for every square-free multi-index $\mathbf b$ there are natural isomorphisms $[W_i(\Delta)]_{\mathbf b}\cong\operatorname{Tor}^{S}_{|\mathbf b|-i}(k,k[\Delta])_{\mathbf b}\cong\widetilde H^{i-1}(\Delta_{\mathbf b};k)^\vee$, yielding its multigraded Hilbert series by summing these cohomology dimensions.

title: Xin Fu (joint with Tseleung So
note: Xin Fu (joint with Tseleung So, Jongbaek Song, and Stephen Theriault), the integral cohomology ring determines the away-from-small-primes homotopy type of quasitoric manifolds over products of equal-dimensional simplices. Key computation: if $M,N$ are $2n$-manifolds over $\prod_{i=1}^{\ell}\Delta^d$ and $H^*(M)\cong H^*(N)$, the fibration $\prod_{i=1}^{\ell}S^{2d+1}\to M\to BT^{m-n}$ gives $\operatorname{skel}_{2d}(M)\simeq\operatorname{skel}_{2d}(BT^{m-n})\simeq\operatorname{skel}_{2d}(N)$; for $k>d$, the attaching map homomorphism $g_M:H_{2k+2}(M)\to\pi_{2k+1}(\operatorname{skel}_{2k}M)$ is an isomorphism after inverting all primes $p\le n/d+1$, so induction over even skeleta yields $M\simeq N$ with those primes inverted.

title: Shintar\^o Kuroki (joint with Yael Karshon)
note: Shintar\^o Kuroki (joint with Yael Karshon), locally standard torus actions are classified up to equivariant diffeomorphism by an orbit manifold, its unimodular facet labeling, and a Chern class. Key computation: to $T^d\curvearrowright M$ one assigns $Q=M/T$, $\widehat\lambda:\partial_1^\circ Q\to(t_{\mathbb Z})_{\mathrm{primitive}}/\{\pm1\}$, and $c\in H^2(Q;t_{\mathbb Z})$; the exact sequence $0\to t_{\mathbb Z}\to\mathbb R^d\to T^d\to0$, together with $H^q(\mathring Q;\mathbb R^d)=0$ and $Q\simeq\mathring Q$, identifies $H^1(\mathring Q;T^d)\cong H^2(Q;t_{\mathbb Z})$, so the free principal bundle $M_{\mathrm{free}}\to\mathring Q$ is recovered from $c$, and the functor $\mathrm{Cl}(M)=(Q,\widehat\lambda,c)$ is full and essentially surjective.

title: Tao Gong
note: Tao Gong, the quotient of a toric variety attached to a Weyl polytope is homotopy equivalent to the toric variety attached to the quotient polytope, for every Lie type and every parabolic subgroup. Key computation: writing $X_P/W\cong(S_N\times(P\cap C))/\!\sim_{\mathrm{ed}}$ and $X_{P/W}\cong(S_N\times(P\cap C))/\!\sim$, the identity on representatives induces $\Phi:X_P/W\to X_{P/W}$; if $p\in\operatorname{relint}(H_I\cap F_J\cap C)$, then $\Phi^{-1}([t,p])\cong\bigl(S_N(\sigma_{[n],p})/S_N(\sigma_p)\bigr)/W_I\cong\bigl(\operatorname{Span}\{\alpha_i:i\in I\}/S_{P^\vee_{I,J}}\bigr)/W_I$, a locally contractible finite-affine quotient, so Smale's theorem gives $\Phi\simeq$ a homotopy equivalence; the same argument yields $X_P/W_K\simeq X_{P/W_K}$.

title: Seonghyeon Yu (joint with Suyoung Choi and Younghan Yoon)
note: Seonghyeon Yu (joint with Suyoung Choi and Younghan Yoon), the rational homology of the real toric varieties associated with the exceptional Weyl groups $E_7$ and $E_8$ is computed explicitly. Key computation: the Weyl-equivariant decomposition $H^*(X_R^{\mathbb R})\cong\bigoplus_{S\in\operatorname{Row}(\Lambda_R)}\widetilde H^{*-1}(K_S)$ reduces the problem to orbit representatives of induced subcomplexes; their computed reduced Betti numbers give $(\beta_0,\ldots,\beta_4)(X_{E_7}^{\mathbb R};\mathbb Q)=(1,63,8127,131041,122976)$ and $(\beta_0,\ldots,\beta_4)(X_{E_8}^{\mathbb R};\mathbb Q)=(1,120,103815,6925200,23932800)$, with all other $\beta_k$ equal to zero.

title: Tyler Schulz (joint with Marcelo Laca)
note: Tyler Schulz (joint with Marcelo Laca), for $0<\beta\le1$ the right $ax+b$ system has a simplex of KMS$_\beta$ states parametrized by probability measures on $\mathbb N^\times\cup\{\infty\}$, whose finite-point extremals generate type $\mathrm{III}_1$ factors. Key computation: every KMS$_\beta$ state factors through $C(X)$ with $X\cong\varprojlim_{a\mid b}X_a$, $X_a=\mathbb T\times\Delta_a$, and transition maps $f_{a,b}(z,d)=(z^{d/\gcd(a,d)},\gcd(a,d))$; the extremal $\psi_{n,\beta}$ further factors through equivariant $*$-homomorphisms $\mathcal T(\mathbb N^\times\ltimes\mathbb Z)\to\mathcal T(\mathbb N^\times\ltimes(\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z))\to C_{\mathbb Q}$, where the intermediate quotient imposes $U^n=1$, producing the Dirac parameter $\delta_n$ and its type $\mathrm{III}_1$ GNS factor.

title: Roberto Hern\'andez Palomares (joint with Brent Nelson)
note: Roberto Hern\'andez Palomares (joint with Brent Nelson), irreducible $C^*$-discrete inclusions are precisely reduced crossed products by outer unitary tensor-category actions and therefore admit a categorical standard invariant. Key computation: for a faithful expectation $E:A\subset B$, the canonical correspondence has $\langle b_1\mid b_2\rangle_A=E(b_1^*b_2)$ and the algebraic discrete part decomposes as $B_\diamond\cong\bigoplus_{K\in\operatorname{Irr}(\operatorname{Bim}_{\mathrm{fgp}}(A))}K\otimes\operatorname{Hom}_{A-A}(K,B\Omega)$; the condition $\overline{B_\diamond}^{\|\cdot\|_B}=B$ and $A'\cap B=\mathbb C$ is equivalent to data $F:\mathcal C\curvearrowright A$, $\mathbf B\in C^*\!\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal C)$ with $A\subset B\cong A\subset A\rtimes_{F,r}\mathbf B$, as illustrated by $\mathcal O_n\cong\operatorname{UHF}_{n^\infty}\rtimes_{F_1,r}\mathbb C[\mathbb Z]$.

title: Marie-France Vign\'eras (joint with Guy Henniart)
note: Marie-France Vign\'eras (joint with Guy Henniart), an admissible representation of $\operatorname{GL}_n(D)$ is, near the identity, an integral combination of parabolically induced trivial representations, making the growth of Moy--Prasad invariants polynomial and identifying its Gelfand--Kirillov dimension. Key computation: for $\operatorname{char}C\ne p$, $\pi\sim\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}c_\lambda(\pi)\operatorname{ind}_{P_\lambda}^{G}\mathbf1$ on a sufficiently small open subgroup; nilpotent orbits correspond to partitions with $\dim_F\mathcal O_\lambda=2d^2\sum_{i<j}\lambda_i\lambda_j$, and hence $\dim_CV^{G_{x,r+i/d}}=Q_{\pi,x,r}(p^i)$ where $Q_{\pi,x,r}(X)=\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}c_\lambda(\pi)|P_\lambda\backslash G/G_{x,r}|X^{fd\,d(\lambda)}$, yielding $\dim_{\mathrm{GK}}\pi=fd\max\{d(\lambda):c_\lambda(\pi)\ne0\}$.

title: Zhizhang Xie (joint work with Jinmin Wang and Guoliang Yu)
note: Zhizhang Xie (joint work with Jinmin Wang and Guoliang Yu), a Fredholm index theorem for a twisted Dirac operator on a polyhedron proves Gromov's flat-corner domination theorem and hence Stoker's conjecture in every dimension. Key computation: for the boundary condition induced by $(\omega\otimes\omega)(c(e_n)\otimes c(e_n))$ and $0<\theta_{ij}(g)\le\theta_{ij}(g_0)<\pi$, the operator $D_B$ is essentially self-adjoint Fredholm with $\operatorname{Ind}(D_B)=\chi(P)=1$; locally the link operator has spectrum $\{-\tfrac12+k\pi/\alpha:k\in\mathbb Z\}$ and $|P_B|\ge\tfrac12$, while the integrated estimate $0=\int_P|D\phi|^2\ge\int_P|\nabla\phi|^2+\int_P\tfrac{\operatorname{Sc}_g}{4}|\phi|^2+\sum_i\int_{F_i}\tfrac{H_g}{2}|\phi|^2+\tfrac12\sum_{i,j}\int_{F_i\cap F_j}(\theta_{ij}(g_0)-\theta_{ij}(g))|\phi|^2$ forces flatness and equality of face and dihedral data.

title: Damien Tageddine
note: Damien Tageddine, matrix spectral triples attached to finer triangulations converge to the classical Dirac and Laplace operators on a compact Riemannian manifold. Key computation: the inductive-limit algebra satisfies $\varprojlim\operatorname{Spec}(A_i)\simeq\operatorname{Spec}(\varinjlim A_i)$ and $Z(A_\infty)\simeq C(M)$, while for the lattice Dirac operator $D_n=\sum_{k=1}^d1\otimes\cdots\otimes D_n^{(k)}\otimes\cdots\otimes1$ one has $\sigma_{A_\infty}([D_\infty,a])=\bigcup_i\sigma_{A_i}([D_i,a_i])$ and $\|[D_\infty,a]\|=\|d_ca\|_\infty$; with sampled points and $\hbar_n=n^{-\alpha}$, the explicit averages $\widehat S_{n\hbar_n}(a)=n^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^n e_k[D_{X_k},a_k]e_k^*$ and $\Omega_{\hbar_n}^n(a)$ converge in probability to $[D,a]$ and $\Delta_Ma$, respectively.

title: Judith Packer (joint work with Carla Farsi
note: Judith Packer (joint work with Carla Farsi, Therese-Marie Landry, Nadia Larsen, and Fr\'ed\'eric Latr\'emoli\`ere), spectral triples on noncommutative solenoids arise as inductive limits of rotation-algebra triples and converge in spectral propinquity. Key computation: for $\Gamma=\mathbb Z[1/p]^2$, the proper bounded-doubling length $L_p(r_1,r_2)=\max\{\|(r_1,r_2)\|_2,p^{\operatorname{scale}(r_1,r_2)}\}$ defines the metric triple $(C^*(\Gamma,\sigma_\theta),\ell^2(\Gamma),D_{L_p})$; moreover $A_\theta\cong\varinjlim(A_{\theta_{2n}},\varphi_n)$ with $\varphi_n(U_{2n})=U_{2n+2}^p$ and $\varphi_n(V_{2n})=V_{2n+2}^p$, and for $D=M_{L_H}\otimes\gamma_1+M_F\otimes\gamma_2$ the finite-stage triples satisfy $\lim_{n\to\infty}\Lambda^{\mathrm{spec}}((C^*(\Gamma_n,\sigma),\ell^2(\Gamma_n)\otimes\mathbb C^2,D_n),(C^*(\Gamma,\sigma),\ell^2(\Gamma)\otimes\mathbb C^2,D))=0$.

title: Piotr M
note: Piotr M. Hajac (joint work with Mariusz Tobolski), suitable graph and path homomorphisms make Leavitt path algebras contravariant and graph $C^*$-algebras covariant, yielding pushout-to-pullback theorems for quantum spaces. Key computation: for a proper target-bijective graph map $f:E\to F$, the induced map $\bar f^*:L_k(F)\to L_k(E)$ is explicitly $[\chi_p]\mapsto\sum_{q\in\bar f^{-1}(p)}[\chi_q]$, defining a contravariant functor; dually, for a path homomorphism satisfying the three regular-monomorphism conditions, $f_*:C^*(E)\to C^*(F)$ is $[\chi_p]\mapsto[\chi_{\bar f(p)}]$, defining a covariant $*$-functor and specializing to the stated pullback constructions for graph models of the equatorial Podle\'s quantum sphere and quantum $\mathbb{CP}^1$.

title: Alfons Van Daele
note: Alfons Van Daele, a locally compact quantum group defined by central Haar weights on a $C^*$-algebra canonically yields a faithful von Neumann algebraic locally compact quantum group. Key computation: a lower-semicontinuous semifinite weight extends by $\widetilde\varphi(x)=\sup_{\omega\le\varphi}\omega(x)$ to a normal weight on $A^{**}$, and Haar invariance $\varphi((\omega\otimes\iota)\Delta(a))=\omega(1)\varphi(a)$ implies that the support projections $e$ and $f$ of the extended left and right weights satisfy $\widetilde\Delta(1-e)(1\otimes(1-e))=0$, hence $f(1-e)=e(1-f)=0$ and $e=f$; cutting down to $M=A^{**}e$ gives $\Delta_0(x)=\widetilde\Delta(x)(e\otimes e)$ with faithful invariant restrictions $\varphi_0,\psi_0$, so $(M,\Delta_0)$ is the associated von Neumann algebraic quantum group.

title: Stevo Todorcevic
note: Stevo Todorcevic, the Ne\v{s}et\v{r}il--R\'odl ordered expansion canonizes finite-arity relations on the random graph and identifies the universal minimal flow of its automorphism group. Key computation: for a finite graph $A$ on $\{0,\ldots,k-1\}$, $C_A=\operatorname{Emb}(A,R)=\{\bar x\in\mathbb N^{(k)}:(i,j)\in E_A\Longleftrightarrow(x_i,x_j)\in R\}$ splits under a homogeneous order $<^*$ into $C_A^\sigma=\{\bar x\in C_A:x_{\sigma(0)}<^*\cdots<^*x_{\sigma(k-1)}\}$; every $S\subseteq\mathbb N^{(k)}$ is constant on each $C_A^\sigma$ after restriction to an arbitrarily large finite induced subgraph, all $k!$ classes remain essential, and this Ramsey-plus-ordering computation makes the natural action $\operatorname{Aut}(R)\curvearrowright\operatorname{LO}(\mathbb N)$ minimal and universal.

title: Morris Ang
note: Morris Ang, Gaussian multiplicative chaos constructs Liouville quantum gravity surfaces and the DOZZ three-point function computes the universal critical-percolation three-point connectivity constant. Key computation: for $0<\gamma<2$, $A_h^\gamma(dz)=\lim_{\varepsilon\to0}\varepsilon^{\gamma^2/2}e^{\gamma h_\varepsilon(z)}dz$ obeys $A_{h+f}^\gamma=e^{\gamma f}A_h^\gamma$ and $f_*A_h^\gamma=A_{\widetilde h}^\gamma$ under $h=\widetilde h\circ f+(2/\gamma+\gamma/2)\log|f'|$; the resulting DOZZ correlation proves the Delfino--Viti formula $P_3(z_1,z_2,z_3)/\sqrt{P_2(z_1,z_2)P_2(z_2,z_3)P_2(z_3,z_1)}=\bigl[C_{\sqrt{8/3}}^{\mathrm{DOZZ}}(7\sqrt6/12,7\sqrt6/12,7\sqrt6/12)\bigr]^{-1}\times(\text{explicit Gamma factors})\approx1.022$.

title: Liat Kessler (joint work with Pranav Chakravarthy
note: Liat Kessler (joint work with Pranav Chakravarthy, River Chiang, and Martin Pinsonnault), equivariant symplectic blowups of a Hamiltonian circle four-manifold at a fixed component are connected from deformation to isotopy using decorated-graph classification and inflation. Key computation: an embedded $J$-holomorphic surface $Z$ produces $J$-taming forms in the classes $[\omega_t]=[\omega]+t\lambda\operatorname{PD}[Z]$ for $0\le\lambda<T$, where $T=\infty$ if $Z\cdot Z\ge0$ and $T=\omega(Z)/(-Z\cdot Z)$ otherwise; applying this family inflation to two $S^1$-equivariant blowups of equal size, whose Karshon decorated graphs coincide, changes the invariant deformation to a cohomologous path, and equivariant Moser then writes $\omega_t=\phi_t^*\omega_0$, giving equivariant isotopy.

title: Zhi L\'u (joint work with Wei Wang)
note: Zhi L\'u (joint work with Wei Wang), equivariant cohomology Chern numbers form a complete system of invariants for unitary $T^k$-bordism, and mixed equivariant characteristic numbers separate equivariant Hamiltonian bordism. Key computation: the universal toric genus $\Phi:\Omega_*^{U,T^k}\to MU^*(BT^k)$ is tested by the Kronecker pairing $\langle\Phi([M]_{T^k}),[f:N\to BT^k]\rangle=[\widetilde f^*(ET^k\times_{T^k}M)]\in MU_*=\Omega_*^U$; the stable tangent splitting $T\widetilde f^*(ET^k\times_{T^k}M)\cong\pi'^*TN\oplus\widetilde f^*(ET^k\times_{T^k}TM)$ expresses every Chern number through equivariant Chern numbers of $M$, so their vanishing kills every pairing, gives $\Phi([M]_{T^k})=0$, and injectivity of $\Phi$ yields $[M]_{T^k}=0$.

title: Stevo Todorcevic
note: Stevo Todorcevic, analytic $n^*$-gaps have a finite basis of minimal equivalence types, obtained by canonizing their tree presentations. Key computation: for gaps $\Gamma$ on $N$ and $\Delta$ on $M$, $\Gamma\le\Delta$ is witnessed by an injection $\phi:N\to M$ carrying $\Gamma_i$ into $\Delta_i$ and $\Gamma_i^\perp$ into $\Delta_i^\perp$; the tree partition theorem produces, from any non-separated analytic family $\Gamma=\{\Gamma_i:i<n\}$, a permutation $\varepsilon:n\to n$ and injection $u:n^{<\omega}\to N$ with $u[X]\in\Gamma_{\varepsilon(i)}$ for every chain $X$ of type $[i]$, reducing every analytic gap to one of finitely many minimal types--exactly five for $n=2$ up to permutation--and yielding the sharp intersection numbers $J(1),\ldots,J(7)=1,8,61,480,3881,31976,266981$.

title: Jeff Achter
note: Jeff Achter, cyclic covers turn moduli of genus-$4$ curves, plane quartics, and five marked points on $\mathbb P^1$ into arithmetic period maps to unitary Shimura varieties. Key computation: for a canonical genus-$4$ curve $C=Q\cap S\subset\mathbb P^3$, the triple cover $v:Z\to Q$ branched along $C$ is a K3 surface; the inverse images $N_i=v^{-1}(M_i)$ of the two rulings satisfy $(N_1,N_2)=3$, so $U(3)=\mathbb ZN_1+\mathbb ZN_2\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Pic}(Z)$ and the deck $\mu_3$-action produces $(Z,\alpha,\rho)\in\mathcal R_{(L_4,\chi_4)}$. Over $\mathbb Z[\zeta_3,1/6]$, $\kappa_4:\mathcal R_{(L_4,\chi_4)}\to\mathcal N_4$ induces an isomorphism on coarse moduli spaces and $\tau_4$ is an open immersion into $\operatorname{Sh}(L_4,\chi_4)$.

title: Yousheng Shi
note: Yousheng Shi, derived intersections of Kudla--Rapoport divisors on ramified unitary Rapoport--Zink spaces equal a corrected derivative of local representation densities in ranks $n\le3$. Key computation: blowing up the isolated singularities of $\mathcal N_n^{\mathrm{Pap}}$ gives the regular semistable Kr\'amer model $\mathcal N_n^{\mathrm{Kra}}$, and for $L=\langle x_1,\ldots,x_n\rangle$ the intersection is $\operatorname{Int}(L)=\chi(\mathcal N_n,\mathcal O_{\mathcal Z(x_1)}\otimes^{\mathbf L}\cdots\otimes^{\mathbf L}\mathcal O_{\mathcal Z(x_n)})$.
